posts.text:
Agent 跑几个小时已经不算稀奇，难的是几个小时之后，它还记得目标、保得住进度，最后真的把事情交付完整。

浙大、蚂蚁等团队这篇 OneDayAgent，研究的就是这种「一天尺度」的长时任务。

面对工作、学习和生活中的开放任务，它会先把目标拆成边界清晰的子任务，同时始终保留用户最初的要求。

执行过程中，只把关键结果和文件作为 checkpoint 留下来，避免完整轨迹不断挤占上下文。

全部执行结束后，系统还会重新对照原始需求做一次全局验收。发现缺失，就只修对应部分，不需要整条任务重新跑。

在 104 个任务里，有 9 个在最终检查时发现问题，其中 6 个经过 repair 被救了回来。长任务里，「Agent 觉得做完了」和真正完成交付，经常还有一段距离。

最终，OneDayAgent + GLM-5.2 在 AgentIF-OneDay 上达到 0.821。同一套 harness 换到 Gemini、Qwen 等 5 个后端模型也能直接运行。

所以任务拉长到几个小时以后，模型能力只是其中一部分。进度怎么保存、上下文怎么交接、最后怎么验收，开始直接决定 Agent 能不能把事情真正做完。

长时 Agent 拼到最后，越来越像在做一套靠谱的项目管理系统。

Introducing ExtractBench, the most comprehensive benchmark for information extraction from complex enterprise documents.

The latest models are pushing the frontier of coding and knowledge work, but surprisingly they still struggle on complex doc extraction tasks in production. A well-tuned extractor must parse multi-page filings without dropping rows, emit exact spatial citations for auditability, and handle messy scans. Also they must do all of this at a viable per-page cost so that you can scale this to millions of docs in production (you can’t be paying upwards of $1 in tokens per page!)

Existing extraction benchmarks fall short: they are not large/diverse enough in document domain (finance, energy, gov, auto), elements (long records, scans, grounding), and schemas.

So our applied research team built ExtractBench.

We evaluated 14 systems: frontier VLMs, coding agents, and specialized extraction APIs, against 370 enterprise documents: 4,869 pages, 67 document types.

Our biggest finding 🧪: Short documents mask critical system flaws. On files past 50 pages, commercial VLMs collapse below 35% recall due to silent list truncation. They hold high precision, but lose output attention and drop most of the table rows.

ExtractBench evaluates value accuracy, long-record completeness, spatial grounding, and per-page cost with zero LLM judges. It is 100% deterministic and reproducible.

In tandem with ExtractBench, we’re also introducing 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗣𝗹𝘂𝘀, a new Extract tier in LlamaParse that debuts at #1 on the leaderboard: 95.6% value accuracy, at less than a third the cost of the closest peer.

posts.translationZh:
推出 ExtractBench，面向复杂企业文档信息抽取的最全面基准。

最新模型正在推动编码和知识工作的前沿，但令人意外的是，它们在生产中的复杂文档抽取任务上仍然表现吃力。一个调优良好的抽取器必须能解析多页申报文件而不漏行，输出精确的空间引用以便审计，并处理凌乱的扫描件。同时，它们还必须以可行的每页成本完成这一切，才能扩展到生产中的数百万份文档（你不能每页花超过 1 美元的 token 成本！）

现有抽取基准仍有不足：在文档领域（金融、能源、政府、汽车）、元素（长记录、扫描件、定位）和 schema 方面不够大、不够多样。

因此，我们的应用研究团队构建了 ExtractBench。

我们评估了 14 个系统：前沿 VLM、编码代理和专门的抽取 API，对照 370 份企业文档：4,869 页、67 种文档类型。

我们的最大发现 🧪：短文档会掩盖关键系统缺陷。对于超过 50 页的文件，商业 VLM 因静默列表截断导致召回率跌破 35%。它们保持了高精度，但失去输出注意力，漏掉了大多数表格行。

ExtractBench 评估值准确率、长记录完整性、空间定位和每页成本，不使用任何 LLM 裁判。它 100% 确定且可复现。

在推出 ExtractBench 的同时，我们还发布了 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗣𝗹𝘂𝘀，这是 LlamaParse 中新的 Extract 层，首次亮相即登上排行榜第 1：值准确率 95.6%，成本不到最接近竞品的三分之一。

quotedTweet.text:
Introducing ExtractBench, the most comprehensive benchmark for information extraction from complex enterprise documents.

The latest models are pushing the frontier of coding and knowledge work, but surprisingly they still struggle on complex doc extraction tasks in production. A well-tuned extractor must parse multi-page filings without dropping rows, emit exact spatial citations for auditability, and handle messy scans. Also they must do all of this at a viable per-page cost so that you can scale this to millions of docs in production (you can’t be paying upwards of $1 in tokens per page!)

Existing extraction benchmarks fall short: they are not large/diverse enough in document domain (finance, energy, gov, auto), elements (long records, scans, grounding), and schemas.

So our applied research team built ExtractBench.

We evaluated 14 systems: frontier VLMs, coding agents, and specialized extraction APIs, against 370 enterprise documents: 4,869 pages, 67 document types.

Our biggest finding 🧪: Short documents mask critical system flaws. On files past 50 pages, commercial VLMs collapse below 35% recall due to silent list truncation. They hold high precision, but lose output attention and drop most of the table rows.

ExtractBench evaluates value accuracy, long-record completeness, spatial grounding, and per-page cost with zero LLM judges. It is 100% deterministic and reproducible.

In tandem with ExtractBench, we’re also introducing 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗣𝗹𝘂𝘀, a new Extract tier in LlamaParse that debuts at #1 on the leaderboard: 95.6% value accuracy, at less than a third the cost of the closest peer.

推出 ExtractBench，面向复杂企业文档信息抽取的最全面基准。

最新模型正在推动编码和知识工作的前沿，但令人意外的是，它们在生产中的复杂文档抽取任务上仍然表现吃力。一个调优良好的抽取器必须能解析多页申报文件而不漏行，输出精确的空间引用以便审计，并处理凌乱的扫描件。同时，它们还必须以可行的每页成本完成这一切，才能扩展到生产中的数百万份文档（你不能每页花超过 1 美元的 token 成本！）

现有抽取基准仍有不足：在文档领域（金融、能源、政府、汽车）、元素（长记录、扫描件、定位）和 schema 方面不够大、不够多样。

这个提醒我很认同，因为我自己平时也经常用这种「对抗式审计」。

通常是 Fable 先写代码，再让 GPT-5.6 Sol 单独 Review，专门去找潜在的 Bug、边界问题和遗漏。大多数时候确实能发现不少问题。

但我也遇到过另一种情况：Review Agent 只是觉得某段代码「看起来有问题」，实际上原来的实现是对的。结果顺着它的建议改下去，反而把正确代码改坏了。

所以现在我会更在意 Review 给出的结论能不能被测试或者被其他证据验证。

现在想让两个模型互相挑错很容易，难的是判断这次修改到底有没有让系统变得更好。

quotedTweet.text:
when you ask an LLM to audit your code, it is essentially answering: "does this code have some pattern that *looks like* a bug?" this is important because many things can "look like" a bug, while still being correct. and "fixing" something that is correct will make it incorrect.

I've ran an experiment where I set up a loop:
- GPT 5.6 Pro audits an algorithm
- Fable 5 to fixes the bugs GPT found
- repeat
with a catch: the algorithm was *already correct* (literally, proven so). the result is complete degradation: in the first iterations, the correct algorithm becomes incorrect. in the next iterations, the (now incorrect) algorithm gets patched. but the patches introduce new cases and bugs. this keeps going until the code is destroyed.

so, a naive loop where a model audits its own code ("adversarially") and then fixes it will lead to failure. of course, as LLMs get smarter, *looks like* a bug will converge to being equivalent, in practically 100% of the cases, to finding a real bug. I think we're very close to that, and it will be interesting when the error rate is so low that these loops start working. but, as of 2026, we're not quite there yet
quotedTweet.translationZh:
当你让 LLM 审计代码时，它本质上是在回答：“这段代码是否有某种*看起来像* bug 的模式？”这一点很重要，因为很多东西可能“看起来像” bug，但实际上仍然是正确的。而“修复”正确的东西会让它变错。

我做了一个实验，设置了一个循环：
- GPT 5.6 Pro 审计算法
- Fable 5 修复 GPT 找到的 bug
- 重复
但有个关键点：这个算法*本来就是正确的*（字面意义上，已被证明正确）。结果是彻底退化：在最初几轮迭代中，正确算法变得不正确。接下来的迭代里，这个（已经错误的）算法被继续打补丁。但补丁又引入新的情况和 bug。如此循环，直到代码被毁掉。

所以，一个让模型“对抗式”审计自己的代码、再修复它的朴素循环会导致失败。当然，随着 LLMs 变得更聪明，*看起来像* bug 会在几乎 100% 的实际情况下收敛为真正的 bug。我认为我们已经非常接近了；当错误率低到这些循环开始奏效时，会很有意思。但截至 2026 年，我们还没完全到那一步

posts.text:
The key is "can you train the target skill in digital-only environments with verifiable reward signals" -- math is the canonical example of this.

If you can, then you can achieve arbitrary levels of skill. So if you define "AGI" as "high skill" (I don't), and you only look at this particular type of programmatically verifiable skill, then you can say we have AGI.

Importantly there are very few end-to-end human jobs that verify both constraints. Almost all jobs have many non-verifiable components, in particular the job of a software engineer. So you can't use this type of AI to replace humans wholesale.

There is some room to weaken the "verifiable" constraint in the future (via synthetic verification) as well as the "digital only" constraint (via simulations). So maybe things will change.

reviewedPosts.text:
Introducing ExtractBench, the most comprehensive benchmark for information extraction from complex enterprise documents.

The latest models are pushing the frontier of coding and knowledge work, but surprisingly they still struggle on complex doc extraction tasks in production. A well-tuned extractor must parse multi-page filings without dropping rows, emit exact spatial citations for auditability, and handle messy scans. Also they must do all of this at a viable per-page cost so that you can scale this to millions of docs in production (you can’t be paying upwards of $1 in tokens per page!)

Existing extraction benchmarks fall short: they are not large/diverse enough in document domain (finance, energy, gov, auto), elements (long records, scans, grounding), and schemas.

So our applied research team built ExtractBench.

We evaluated 14 systems: frontier VLMs, coding agents, and specialized extraction APIs, against 370 enterprise documents: 4,869 pages, 67 document types.

Our biggest finding 🧪: Short documents mask critical system flaws. On files past 50 pages, commercial VLMs collapse below 35% recall due to silent list truncation. They hold high precision, but lose output attention and drop most of the table rows.

ExtractBench evaluates value accuracy, long-record completeness, spatial grounding, and per-page cost with zero LLM judges. It is 100% deterministic and reproducible.

In tandem with ExtractBench, we’re also introducing 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗣𝗹𝘂𝘀, a new Extract tier in LlamaParse that debuts at #1 on the leaderboard: 95.6% value accuracy, at less than a third the cost of the closest peer.

Explore the findings, download the dataset, or run the harness:

Blog: 
https://t.co/tsXfovKJaz
GitHub: https://t.co/auzmOGgUl3
HuggingFace: https://t.co/1eKisSBrE8

We will be actively evolving both our extraction benchmark as well as our extraction harness over time. 

If you check out either ExtractBench or LlamaParse, let us know your feedback!

Agent 跑几个小时已经不算稀奇，难的是几个小时之后，它还记得目标、保得住进度，最后真的把事情交付完整。

浙大、蚂蚁等团队这篇 OneDayAgent，研究的就是这种「一天尺度」的长时任务。

面对工作、学习和生活中的开放任务，它会先把目标拆成边界清晰的子任务，同时始终保留用户最初的要求。

执行过程中，只把关键结果和文件作为 checkpoint 留下来，避免完整轨迹不断挤占上下文。

全部执行结束后，系统还会重新对照原始需求做一次全局验收。发现缺失，就只修对应部分，不需要整条任务重新跑。

在 104 个任务里，有 9 个在最终检查时发现问题，其中 6 个经过 repair 被救了回来。长任务里，「Agent 觉得做完了」和真正完成交付，经常还有一段距离。

最终，OneDayAgent + GLM-5.2 在 AgentIF-OneDay 上达到 0.821。同一套 harness 换到 Gemini、Qwen 等 5 个后端模型也能直接运行。

所以任务拉长到几个小时以后，模型能力只是其中一部分。进度怎么保存、上下文怎么交接、最后怎么验收，开始直接决定 Agent 能不能把事情真正做完。

长时 Agent 拼到最后，越来越像在做一套靠谱的项目管理系统。

The key is "can you train the target skill in digital-only environments with verifiable reward signals" -- math is the canonical example of this.

If you can, then you can achieve arbitrary levels of skill. So if you define "AGI" as "high skill" (I don't), and you only look at this particular type of programmatically verifiable skill, then you can say we have AGI.

Importantly there are very few end-to-end human jobs that verify both constraints. Almost all jobs have many non-verifiable components, in particular the job of a software engineer. So you can't use this type of AI to replace humans wholesale.

There is some room to weaken the "verifiable" constraint in the future (via synthetic verification) as well as the "digital only" constraint (via simulations). So maybe things will change.
